subject: CloudKey activation: feature gating & SLA exception request

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Kar thik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: CloudKey ask: version pin + warm pool SLA exception (requested by VP Eng)

Team — quick heads up from my call with CloudKey just now. Alex Zhou (VP Eng) asked for two explicit asks to close the deal this quarter:

1) A feature-gating option so they can pin their production routing to a specific model variant (quantized 4-bit) for 6 months, with a documented rollback path.
2) A short-term SLA exception that guarantees warm-pool capacity for peak windows during the first 90 days post-activation (they plan a phased rollout).

They've pushed timeline: pilot starts in mid-Oct; GA-ish by end of Nov. They want a signed SOW that mentions the pin and warm-pool language. Attached is the SOW I drafted with legal comments and a proposed activation timeline (activation_timeline.xlsx).

Can product/eng confirm feasibility and an engineering ETA? Also need clear gating controls we can promise in-contract (e.g., API param + account-level setting) and any telemetry/audit obligations.

Related notes: Deal size ~ $420k ARR first-year commit if we deliver the pilot/GA schedule. HubSpot: CK-2027-045.

Thanks — Ben

--

Ben — thanks, appreciate the context. A few clarifying questions before I talk to legal and prioritize in the next roadmap sync: 

- By "pin to a specific model variant" do they mean a model SHA or an approximate artifact (e.g., "quantized-v1-4bit")? Need to know if they require immutable deployment guarantees (no live model upgrades) or just routing preference with an allowed fallback path.
- Warm-pool guarantee: are they expecting hard reservations (dedicated GPUs) or a soft warm pool (higher burst priority)? If hard reservation, we need to align with capacity planning and pricing.
- Audit/telemetry: what level of traceability do they want? Full token-level logging, or event-level (inference start/end + model id)?

If they need model immutability + dedicated capacity for 90 days, that is a material engineering effort and a commercial commitment. If they accept routing preference + automatic fallback, we can likely deliver config and gating in 2-3 sprints (assuming no infra blockers).

Ben, can you confirm Alex's exact ask on immutability vs preference, and whether procurement/legal already signaled any specific compliance language?

-Karthik

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: CloudKey ask: version pin + warm pool SLA exception (requested by VP Eng)

Karthik / Ben — technical take:

- Pinning: We can support a pin by exposing an account-level "model_affinity" flag that overrides routing and prefers a specific model artifact. That can be implemented as a config entry plus a routing check; fallback rules would need to be explicit (e.g., degrade to compatible quantized variant or route to hosted fallback). Implement/QA estimate: 3 sprints (6 weeks) to ship a hardened control with UI + API, assuming we don't need cross-region affinity.

- Immutability: preventing live upgrades is harder. We can restrict automatic model rollouts for a tenant (i.e., disable auto-update), but preventing manual operator changes (entirely) requires an audit + approval workflow — adds 2 more sprints.

- Warm-pool: we have two options: soft warm-pool (prioritized queuing + pre-warm KV caches) which is low-risk and doable in 2 weeks, or hard reservations (dedicated capacity) which requires capacity commit and pricing changes. Soft warm-pool + observability hooks should meet a lot of their risk profile.

Risks: audit/export requirements (token-level logs) have privacy/cost implications — need legal sign-off and a retention SLA. Also need confirmation on expected peak qps and model latency targets; our capacity planning depends on those numbers.

I'll sketch a short RFC and drop it in the Drive folder (see link). If leadership wants a faster commit we need an Exec-level note on capacity tradeoffs.

-Markus

--

Adding CS perspective:

- CloudKey's rollout plan (shared during the call) covers a staged 3-month ramp with predictable daily peaks (mostly 09:00-11:00 PT). They will start with ~250 users internal/alpha and ramp to ~3k requests/min at GA. Ben, can you confirm these numbers with Alex?
- For the pilot, they'd accept a soft warm-pool if it's paired with a short-term incident SLA (faster on-call response window) and automated cache seeding prior to their release windows.
- We should include a runbook and a scheduled playbook for on-call during the first 30 days; CS can staff a runway but needs SRE + Eng on-call escalation paths mapped out.

Operational asks we will require in the SOW: clear escalation contacts, a 2-week test window to validate warm-pool behavior, and mutual rollback criteria. If legal insists on model immutability, we should push for time-limited immutability and explicit change control to reduce long-term ops burden.

I'll update the runbook template and share a link once Ben confirms the traffic profile.

Thanks everyone — good alignment so far. Summary for Exec ask:

- Customer: CloudKey (CK-2027-045), potential $420k ARR first year.
- Asks: account-level model affinity (routing preference) + soft warm-pool guarantee for 90 days; contingency path to dedicated capacity if usage exceeds forecast.
- Recommended commercial posture: include routing preference + soft warm-pool in SOW (we can commit to this without capacity reservation). Add a clause: "dedicated capacity subject to separate SOW and pricing if 4 consecutive weeks of sustained peak > X QPS".
- Engineering impact: 2-3 sprints to ship config + API + UI for affinity; 2 weeks for soft warm-pool + cache-seeding automation.
- Risks: token-level logging or strict immutability increase cost and compliance work.

Action items before we commit to the customer:
1) Ben: confirm expected peak QPS and whether procurement needs immutability language (Alex/Procurement).
2) Karthik/Markus: finalize RFC and a short engineering estimate we can attach to the SOW. Please add the RFC link to the Drive folder.
3) Monica: draft the 30-day runbook + escalation summary to include in SOW.
4) Legal/Finance: review the proposed "dedicated capacity" fallback clause and pricing guardrail (I will loop them once we have the RFC).

Ben — if you can confirm the QPS and whether Alex insists on immutability by EOD tomorrow, I'll escalate to Legal and Ops for a quick review cycle.
